contexts.text: They fed in the sedge () = instruction... The sedge, or larger grass which is near rivers, = the scientifics which are of the natural man... Thus to feed in the sedge = to be instructed in scientifics, and, through scientifics, concerning truths and goods.

That there will no longer be... even natural and sensuous truths, is signified by the reed and sedge shall wither... (). AE 627:9. ( = that all perception of truth and good from the sense of the letter, which otherwise belongs to the sensuous man, will vanish. AE 654:49.)
